## Description
Surface Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (SNMR) is the only&#10;&#9;&#9;noninvasive geophysical method that responds nearly uniquely to water. As the measured&#10;&#9;&#9;EMF is proportional to the proton-precession frequency, which in turn is proportional to&#10;&#9;&#9;the planet’s static magnetic field, SNMR signals are comparatively weak. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;Using small systems of several kilograms and several watts, the exploration depth of &#10;&#9;&#9;SNMR is one to two orders of magnitude smaller than TDEM.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;TDEM can detect water to depths up to a&#9;few kilometers, whereas SNMR is limited to &#10;&#9;&#9;depths of a few tens of meters.&#10;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;https://space.stackexchange.com/questions/8653/how-to-find-underground-resources-water-caves-on-mars&#10;&#9;&#9;https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/pdf/10.1029/2002JE001882
